title: Efficient Key-Homomorphic PRFs
summary: Known key-homomorphic PRF constructions are heavyweight and lack AES-comparable realizations; an efficient construction, a fundamental efficiency lower bound, and exact or non-abelian variants remain open.

formal_statement.body: Known constructions of key-homomorphic pseudorandom functions (PRFs) are seemingly heavyweight for a symmetric-key primitive, and no realization with performance comparable to AES is known. Construct key-homomorphic PRFs with AES-comparable performance, or prove a fundamental lower bound that precludes such efficiency. Additionally, no exact key-homomorphic PRF is currently known in the standard model; construct an exact KHPRF in the standard model from some DDH-like assumption. It also remains open to construct a non-abelian key-homomorphic weak PRF (KHwPRF), or even a non-abelian input-homomorphic weak PRF (IHwPRF), whose security is based on an underlying cryptographic assumption over non-abelian groups.

scope.domain: Symmetric cryptography focused on key-homomorphic pseudorandom functions and related weak or input-homomorphic variants.
assumptions: Some DDH-like assumption for an exact KHPRF in the standard model
An underlying cryptographic assumption over non-abelian groups for the weak variants
parameters: AES-comparable performance as the efficiency benchmark
The standard model as the target model for exact KHPRFs
Non-abelian groups as the algebraic setting for KHwPRFs and IHwPRFs
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct key-homomorphic PRFs with AES-comparable performance or prove a fundamental lower bound precluding that efficiency; construct an exact KHPRF in the standard model from some DDH-like assumption; and construct a non-abelian KHwPRF or IHwPRF whose security is based on an underlying cryptographic assumption over non-abelian groups.

progress.summary: The introduction presents efficient construction or a fundamental efficiency lower bound as a natural question, motivated by heavyweight known constructions and the absence of AES-comparable realizations. It also states open targets for exact standard-model and non-abelian variants.
citation_labels: Navid Alamati et al., Symmetric Primitives with Structured Secrets
